reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch G2-MG-Q1-Harden (mat_g2_mg_q1_0..mat_g2_mg_q1_2), 2026-08-18

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The samples successfully test both composing and decomposing figures as explicitly required by the competency. For instance, "joined along their flat straight edges" and "cut straight down the middle into two 2-by-2 parts" directly address the composition and decomposition of figures.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The generated items cover the full spectrum of shapes listed in the competency, including squares, rectangles, triangles, circles, half-circles, and quarter-circles. They also incorporate both specified contexts: "Using cut-outs" and "On a square grid".

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The questions are well-suited for Grade 2. The scenarios use simple, easily visualizable shapes and operations, like joining "two identical triangles" or "four quarter-circles", which matches the cognitive expectations for a first-quarter Grade 2 learner.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The generator provides a good variety of problem structures. It asks students to identify the resulting shape from composition ("What shape is formed?"\), the resulting shapes from decomposition ("What two shapes are made?"\), and the count of simple shapes in a composite figure ("How many simple shapes were used to compose it?"\).

competency_alignment.rationale: Every question strictly adheres to the competency text. There is no extraneous vocabulary, and the operations are limited entirely to composing and decomposing the exact set of shapes mentioned using "cut-outs" and "square grids".

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The numerical values and spatial dimensions are appropriately scaled. Grid sizes like "4-by-2" and shape counts like "1 square, 1 triangle, and 1 rectangle" are perfectly scaled for Grade 2 mathematics, avoiding overly complex arithmetic.

samples_reviewed.question_text: On a square grid, a composite shape has 1 square, 1 triangle, and 1 rectangle joined together. How many simple shapes were used to compose it?
Using cut-outs, two identical triangles are placed together along their matching edges. What shape can they form?
On a square grid, a composite figure is made by joining 2 squares of 4 grid units each side by side. What shape is formed?
A composite figure is made of a rectangle with a half-circle attached on top. How many simple shapes form this figure?
Using cut-outs, two half-circles are joined along their flat straight edges. What shape is formed?
On a square grid, a 4-by-2 rectangle is cut straight down the middle into two 2-by-2 parts. What shape is each part?
On a square grid, a 4-by-2 rectangle is cut straight down the middle into two 2-by-2 parts. What shape is each part?
On a square grid, a composite shape has 1 square, 1 triangle, and 1 rectangle joined together. How many simple shapes were used to compose it?
On a square grid, a composite figure is made of 1 square, 1 half-circle, and 1 rectangle. How many shapes form this composite figure?
On a square grid, a rotated composite shape is made of a square and a triangle. How many simple shapes make up this figure?
Using cut-outs, a square is cut along a slant from one corner to the opposite corner. What two shapes are made?
Using cut-outs, four quarter-circles of the same size are joined together. What complete shape do they make?
